payload.detail: UPDATE 2026-09-25 from the owner-supplied Ultimate Audit Master Report (audit F10), not reproduced offline: the WebKit phone-chrome failures include header overlay, composer visibility, scroll animation and narrow settings geometry, with one settings position measured at -140 px. Audit recommendation: audit the shared scroll controller, safe-area geometry and scroll-container ownership rather than per-test fixes. The audit duplicate-<main> finding (F08) is already resolved as the hidden streaming clone (#TWS2GD); the Specifiers mobile Axe failure and the Differentials ChunkLoadError are separate rows queued the same day. PRIOR DETAIL: UPDATE 2026-09-20 (six Firefox failures read from the job log of main run 35503893104; four now addressed, two open; no Firefox was run - see the egress row). THE COUNT AND THE CLASSIFICATION IN THIS ROW WERE BOTH WRONG. Firefox failed SIX, not five, and only THREE were tolerance, not five. FIXED AND MERGED (PR #2932): three sub-pixel artefacts - a 16px card gap measured 15.999969482421875, a 12px column gap measured 11.999954223632812, and a 48px tap target measured 47.98333740234375 against its existing 2px allowance. The first two are float error from subtracting two client rects; the third is Firefox storing layout in app units of 1/60 CSS px, so 47.98333740234375 is exactly 2879/60 - one app unit short, the smallest miss the engine can express. tests/helpers/layout-tolerance.ts holds one 0.05px tolerance, mutation-tested from both sides. No floor lowered, nothing skipped or quarantined. FIXED, MERGED as PR #2933 at 0cfdd250e on 2026-09-20, verified as an ancestor of this reconciliation - originally recorded as AWAITING MERGE because the request was queued before it landed: the fourth, ui-on-call-boards dark mode, was TEST ORDERING and not an app bug. It set the colour-scheme override while the page was still on about:blank, and Playwright Firefox does not carry that into the first navigation; the theme is resolved once pre-paint by the bootstrap in src/lib/theme.ts, so a late preference is already missed. PROOF IT IS NOT THE APP: the twelve dark assertions in ui-caring-contacts-workspace.spec.ts PASS on Firefox in this same run (tests 48, 53, 59, 65, 72, 79, 85, 100, 138, 152, 159, 169) and every one navigates first and switches scheme after. An earlier reading blamed color-scheme: light on :root and concluded dark mode was broken for every Firefox and Safari user; those twelve passes refute it. Do not reopen the design-system dark contract on this evidence. STILL OPEN: the remaining two Firefox failures are tracked separately - see the row for the document-viewer hit counter and the tools Forms panel. The eight WebKit failures are UNCHANGED and still unexamined; the six phone-chrome ones remain the likely-real-iPhone-bug reading recorded above. UPDATE 2026-09-20 (read from the GitHub job logs of the latest main release-browser-matrix run; still no local browser run, provisioning fails here as described below). THE COUNT IS 13, NOT 15: Chromium green in ~8 min; Firefox 700 passed / 5 failed in ~28 min; WebKit 696 passed / 8 failed in ~40 min. THE 2026-09-06 CONCLUSION IS HALF WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT OF THIS UPDATE. The Firefox half is tolerance work as recorded — one failure is provably a measurement artefact, Expected >= 12 / Received 11.999954223632812, a sub-pixel rounding difference and nothing more. THE WEBKIT HALF IS NOT. Six of the eight WebKit failures are phone scroll, header, footer and composer behaviour. WebKit is Safari engine, so on an iPhone those are candidate real user-visible bugs, not engine-geometry tolerance, and must be read as a bug report rather than assertion-loosening work. ORDER: fix the five Firefox tolerances first because they are cheap and provably artefacts, then treat the six WebKit phone-chrome failures as a defect investigation, and do that before the tablet row #6GR6B8 because the two are plausibly the same root cause. QUARANTINING IS STILL THE WRONG ANSWER, and more so now: quarantining a phone-chrome failure on Safari engine would hide a defect, not a flake. tests/flake-ledger.json is for REPRODUCED flakes, requires @quarantine in the test title, and expires every entry within 31 days — and it is currently empty by design. NOT FIXED 2026-09-18. WHY IT WAS NOT DONE: the failures are only visible by running Firefox and WebKit, and browser provisioning fails in this environment — scripts/setup-claude-cloud.sh browsers returns 403, no allowlist entry for cdn.playwright.dev. A substitute Chromium exists at /opt/pw-browsers and playwright.config.ts honours PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH, so Chromium work is possible here; the other two engines are not. Sizing this needs a machine that can run all three. Note also that this is the one thing keeping main red, so it will be the first failure the new red-main reporting (#T82ND3) raises. Historical note only: an earlier 2026-09-06 write-up used a 15-failure count and treated the whole set as deterministic geometry differences to loosen; that count and that blanket remedy are superseded by this update and must not be reapplied.
